title: Quantized pipeline throughput/latency sweep across FP8 and INT8 with multi-window batching and KV-warmup
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Produce a reproducible benchmark suite that characterizes tail-latency, median latency, and sustained throughput for FP8 and INT8 model variants across a spectrum of batching policies and long-context workloads. This ticket focuses on interactions between continuous batching windows, KV-cache warmup behavior for long horizons, and the accuracy/quality delta after calibration. Deliverables: 1) experiment harness and scripts that run on both CI and dedicated infra pools; 2) a canonical results dashboard with CSV/JSON exports; 3) a short decision memo recommending default quant profiles and autoscaling knobs for runtime-1.19. Scope: Llama-2 70B-equivalent family (mixed-precision checkpoints we maintain), sequence lengths: 512, 2048, 8192; batch shapes: [1,4,8,16], microbatching enabled; KV warmup patterns: cold start, periodic microbursts, steady-state long horizon. Success criteria: identify configurations that keep 99th-percentile token latency under 250ms for P99-sensitive customers while reducing CPU/GPU token cost at least 1.8x vs FP16 in steady-state for INT8 variants without accuracy regression > 1.5% on the evaluation prompt set.
comments: 2026-02-21: Kickoff notes added. Aligned with Model Onboarding team to reuse the calibration artifacts from ENG-26177 and ENG-31204 (references in dependencies).
2026-02-26: Infra readiness check - dedicated test pool (dgx-8p) available; need permission for burst nodes in stage cluster. Filed infra request INF-4412.

2026-03-02: First run completed for sequence=512, batch=8. Observed unexpected spike in P99 during microburst pattern when KV warmup is disabled. Hypothesis: kernel fallback due to memory fragmentation. Added kernel-level logging in harness.

2026-03-05: Design trade-off discussion with Runtime team: enable aggressive coalescing vs preserve low-latency. Agreed to test two routing policies: conservative (favor latency) and aggressive (favor throughput).

2026-03-08: Accuracy validation completed on eval-set-v3: FP8 variant shows 0.9% delta, INT8 shows 1.6% delta — INT8 exceeds target. Running targeted calibration sweep with per-layer range clipping and quant-aware bias correction.

2026-03-10: Interim results posted to dashboard. Next steps: run full long-window (8192) sweep with microburst replay and confirm autoscale triggers do not amplify tail latencies. Prepare PR for harness additions and a lightweight runbook for on-call (ENG-ops review).
